attack.final_span:
teaches strategy at the undergraduate and graduate level at Washington University in St. Louis. His research extensively uses large datasets from business, political, and governance sectors. He has released six books, edited two, and published 70+ papers. He is often-quoted by various sources, holds the status of a Fellow of the Strategic Management Society (SMS), and is an invited member of the editorial boards of strategic management journals including the Strategic Management Journal, Journal of Management, Organization Science, and multiple other significant strategy journals. He has shown up multiple times on the Bloomberg Business Network to talk about proactive corporate governance and how strategic issues can affect any organization type. Lamar is also widely demanded as a public speaker, delivering the keynote address at the 50th anniversary of the ICIS conference, organized by the University of Sydney.
Lamar holds the position of research faculty for the Loan Office and Retirement Planning Fellowship Program and leads The Brookings Business Executive Education program in mergers and acquisitions as the academic director.
Earlier in his career, Lamar worked as a consultant at Bain & Company’s Boston office. He served as a lead author for articles published in the Harvard Business Review, Business Week, and the Financial Times, and received praise for his contribution to Bain & Company’s 1999 annual report. Apart from his work at Washington University, Lamar has also taught at the Macquarie Graduate School of Management, INSEAD, and the University of Kentucky. He has been an active entrepreneur, involved with three startup companies: Song Swops, Economics, and Boosterfisher Inc. He serves on the editorial board of the Strategic Management Journal, the Journal of Management, the Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization, and the Journal of Organizational Economics.
Lamar earned his Ph.D. in Business Administration from U.C. Berkeley’s Haas School of Business in 2003, along with an M.A. in 2001 and a B.A. in 1997.
